jason-a-s-whitely.name: Jason A. S. Whitely
jason-a-s-whitely.bio: Jason A. S. Whitely is a game composer whose early-1990s credits include Space Hulk and Desert Strike. His music for Space Hulk was used across the Amiga and PC versions, while surviving public biographical information about him is limited.

jason-c-brooke.name: Jason C. Brooke
jason-c-brooke.bio: Jason C. Brooke is an English composer, programmer and sound designer whose C64 work includes a substantial run of arcade conversions and licensed games. He worked with companies including Binary Design and Musicon, where he collaborated with David Whittaker on music technology and production.

jason-page.name: Jason Page
jason-page.bio: Jason Page is an English game composer and sound designer whose career began with home-computer audio and later extended into major console projects. He worked at Graftgold, contributed to C64 and Amiga releases, and later held audio roles at Sony, with credits including music connected to the original Gran Turismo.

jean-baudlot.name: Jean Baudlot
jean-baudlot.bio: Jean Baudlot was a French composer, pianist and songwriter who also became a prominent game musician during the late 1980s and early 1990s. His game work included titles for Ocean France and Delphine Software, with Future Wars and Flashback represented in the CCG Amiga archive.

jeff-minter.name: Jeff Minter
jeff-minter.bio: Jeff Minter is an English programmer and game designer who founded Llamasoft and became one of the most distinctive independent developers of the early home-computer era. His C64 catalogue includes Gridrunner, Hover Bovver, Revenge of the Mutant Camels and Sheep in Space, and he also created music and light-synthesizer software alongside his game design work.

sources.title: Centre for Computing History - Jeff Minter

jeroen-tel.name: Jeroen Tel
jeroen-tel.bio: Jeroen Tel is a Dutch composer who became one of the best-known musicians of the later Commodore 64 era. He co-founded Maniacs of Noise with Charles Deenen in 1987 and produced music for a wide range of games, including Cybernoid, Hawkeye, Myth and Turbo Out Run in the CCG archive.

jim-simmons.name: Jim Simmons
jim-simmons.bio: Jim Simmons is an American game developer and audio contributor whose credits include Cinemaware-era titles on Commodore and Amiga systems. The CCG archive links him to Rocket Ranger, It Came from the Desert and Antheads, with later industry credits extending beyond music into development roles.

johannes-bjerregaard.name: Johannes Bjerregaard
johannes-bjerregaard.bio: Johannes Bjerregaard was a Danish C64 composer and scene musician whose work became highly regarded among other SID musicians. He was associated with groups including DMC, Maniacs of Noise and Soul Syndicate, and the CCG archive links him to Flimbo's Quest and Kamikaze.

john-a-fitzpatrick.name: John A. Fitzpatrick
john-a-fitzpatrick.bio: John A. Fitzpatrick is an American game-audio contributor associated with several mid-1980s Commodore 64 releases. The CCG archive links him to Bruce Lee, The Goonies, Zorro and Barry McGuigan World Championship Boxing; public personal biographical material remains limited.

sources.title: MobyGames and C64 game credit records

john-broomhall.name: John Broomhall
john-broomhall.bio: John Broomhall is an English composer, musician, audio director and game-audio specialist whose career includes senior roles at MicroProse and extensive independent work. His credits include X-COM/UFO: Enemy Unknown, Transport Tycoon, Geoff Crammond’s Grand Prix series and many later productions across music, sound and dialogue.

jon-hare.name: Jon Hare
jon-hare.bio: Jon Hare is an English game designer, artist and musician best known as the co-founder of Sensible Software with Chris Yates. His work includes Sensible Soccer, Cannon Fodder and other major 16-bit releases, where he contributed creatively across design, graphics, music and production.

jonathan-dunn.name: Jonathan Dunn
jonathan-dunn.bio: Jonathan Dunn is an English composer and sound designer best known for his work at Ocean Software. His C64 output includes RoboCop, Platoon, Operation Wolf and many other licensed or arcade-derived games, and he later continued in professional game audio including work connected with Electronic Arts.
